label: Suffering-adjusted days per animal (Ambitious Impact, via ACE)

rows.label: SADs averted per hen-year moved from a battery cage to an aviary
rows.change: a year a hen spends in an aviary instead of a battery cage

source.title: Ambitious Impact SADs, via ACE's Sinergia Animal CEA (2025), 'SADs per animal' tab
source.quote: 28.9 SADs for a battery-caged hen minus 11.5 for an aviary hen
source.note: 2024 SADs: 28.94 = 62.38 intensity-weighted days × Ambitious Impact's 2024 hen weight 0.464 (ACE's ÇHKD sheet, 'SADs Estimate'). Low end: ACE's 7.93 for The Humane League ('Cage-Free Accountability (US, G'!B16), a 2025 SAD figure, restated on the 2024 basis: 7.93 × 0.463966 / 0.347334 = 10.59.

rows.explainer:
How much suffering one laying hen is spared for each year she lives in an aviary instead of a battery cage, in suffering-adjusted days (SADs): days of suffering weighted by pain intensity and by the hen's welfare range.

Best guess: Ambitious Impact's current figures as ACE used them in 2025 (28.9 − 11.5 = 17.49). Low end: the 7.93 ACE used in its 2025 review of The Humane League for the same transition, in ACE's 2025 SADs, which build in a lower hen weight (34.7% of a person against 46.4%); on this fact's 2024 basis it is 10.6. ACE's own models still disagree by 1.7× after that, so models that use this fact carry the disagreement as uncertainty.

The figure has Ambitious Impact's 2024 hen weight built in; the models divide it by that weight.

rows.label: SADs averted per hen-year moved from an enriched cage to an aviary
rows.change: a year a hen spends in an aviary instead of an enriched cage

source.title: ACE, The Humane League CEA (2025), Cage-Free Accountability tab
source.note: 2025 SADs: ACE's 2025 sheets say they use ACE's own 2025 SADs values ('Contextual information'!A2); Animal Welfare Observatory's sheet cites '[Public] ACE - SADs (Suffering-Adjusted Days) 2025' for the same 3.05 ('Cage-Free Eggs CEA'!F26). Models divide it by Ambitious Impact's 2025 hen weight.
source.quote: Assumes hens are being moved from a 'furnished' or 'enriched' cage into an aviary.

rows.explainer:
The same as the cage-to-aviary figure, for hens starting in 'enriched' (furnished) cages, as in the EU since 2012. Smaller because enriched cages are less bad.

The range (half to double) is ours: ACE gives a point value, and the cage-to-aviary figure moved by 2× between ACE's own models.

rows.label: SADs averted per broiler chicken raised under Better Chicken Commitment standards
rows.change: a broiler chicken raised to Better Chicken Commitment standards

source.title: ACE, The Humane League CEA (2025), BCC Accountability tab
source.note: 2025 SADs, as for the enriched-cage figure: models divide it by Ambitious Impact's 2025 hen weight.

rows.explainer:
Suffering averted over one broiler chicken's life (about six weeks) when it is raised to Better Chicken Commitment / European Chicken Commitment standards: slower-growing breeds, more space, enrichment and better slaughter.

ACE uses 0.64 in several 2025 reviews. The range (half to double) is ours; ACE gives no range and notes its SAD values have since been updated.

rows.label: SADs averted per animal-product meal replaced by a plant-based meal
rows.change: a meal replaced by a plant-based one

source.title: ACE, Sinergia Animal CEA (2025), meat reduction tab: 900,203 SADs (86,972–1,713,434) for 997,510 meals
source.note: 2024 SADs (ACE's Sinergia sheet uses the 2024 per-animal SADs: 28.94 per caged hen, 84.55 per sow). Low end: ACE's 0.084 for Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira ('Institutional Meat reduction CE'!B15), from ACE Meal Replacement Estimates 2025 ('Brazil'!L2:L8, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11W1pj0_zi0aHabR_degTMNT4wYpf_HbdMqwFxfEiv5k/edit), 2025 SADs, restated species by species on the 2024 basis with Ambitious Impact's weights (chickens × 1.336, shrimp × 0.934, pigs × 1.227, cattle × 1.156, fish × 1.690): 0.101.

rows.explainer:
Suffering averted when one meal with meat, fish, eggs or dairy is replaced by a plant-based one, through the animals that are no longer bred and raised for it. It depends heavily on what the meal would have contained: a chicken or fish meal involves many more animal-days of suffering than a beef meal.

Best guess and high end: ACE's 2025 Sinergia Animal estimate (0.90 per meal, upper bound 1.72), in 2024 SADs. Low end: the 0.084 ACE used for Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira's institutional meals in the same year, in ACE's 2025 SADs; with the same species weights as the rest of this fact it is 0.10. ACE's own figures differ by 9×, so use a model-specific value only when the charity reports what the replaced meals contained, and say why.

Reference meal: the best guess averages Sinergia's institutional canteen meals across the countries it works in, whose per-country values differ several-fold with the meat species served. To adapt it, scale by the ratio of the charity's meat per meal and species mix to that reference, as input rows with sources.

rows.label: Animals spared per animal-product meal replaced
rows.change: a meal replaced by a plant-based one

source.title: ACE, Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira CEA (2025), Institutional meat reduction tab

rows.explainer: How many animals are no longer raised for each meal replaced. Context only: SADs, not animal counts, are the comparable outcome. Range is ours, roughly halving for beef-heavy diets and up to ACE's other estimates for chicken- and fish-heavy diets.

rows.label: SADs averted per shrimp electrically stunned before slaughter

source.title: ACE, Shrimp Welfare Project CEA (2025), 'Program 1: HSI CEA' tab
source.note: 2025 SADs (ACE's 2025 sheets use its 2025 SADs values; the shrimp weight built in is Ambitious Impact's 2025 one, 0.199). High end: ACE's 2024 Aquatic Life Institute figure, 0.0973 ('SADs Estimate'!B16 = days of pain × 0.97 × 0.3 × 0.62 × 3.18), restated on the 2025 basis: × 0.199089 / 0.186 = 0.104. The × 3.18 is Ambitious Impact's: its cell comment says the multiplier accounts for the exponential growth of the comparative rating of pain types, not yet part of the calculation.

rows.explainer:
Suffering spared when a farmed shrimp is stunned with electricity before slaughter instead of dying slowly in ice slurry or by asphyxiation, in Ambitious Impact's suffering-adjusted days (SADs).

Best guess: the 0.00452 ACE used in its 2025 review of the Shrimp Welfare Project, its most recent figure. High end: the 0.0973 in ACE's 2024 review of the Aquatic Life Institute, from Ambitious Impact's calculation, which assumes 20 minutes of the most intense pain in ice slurry and multiplies by 3.18, Ambitious Impact's stand-in for pain intensity growing exponentially between categories. That figure has the 2024 shrimp weight (18.6%) built in; on this fact's 2025 basis (19.9%) it is 0.104. ACE's figures differ 23-fold for the same change; ACE hasn't said why, so models that use this fact carry that disagreement as uncertainty.

rows.label: Share of a replaced meal's suffering that falls on fish

source.title: ACE, Global meal replacement estimates (2024), 'SADs per year (global)' tab: animals spared per plant-based person per year by group, times SADs per animal (mean of ACE's bounds)
source.note: Wild-caught fishes 78.77 × 19.17 SADs, farmed fishes 13.76 × 78.9, farmed reptiles and amphibians 0.06 × 78.9 (ACE's salmon stand-in): 2,600 of 2,819 SADs a year. These reproduce ACE's 26.9 SADs per animal spared.

rows.explainer:
Which animals a replaced meal spares, by their share of its suffering-adjusted days. Fish dominate: a plant-based diet spares about 79 wild-caught and 14 farmed fish a year against 12 birds and 0.6 mammals, and ACE counts a farmed salmon's life at 79 SADs.

From ACE's 2024 global estimates, the source of its per-meal figures. A particular charity's meals may differ (a beef-heavy canteen spares fewer fish); we use the global mix for every meal model until a charity reports what its meals contained.

rows.label: Share of a replaced meal's suffering that falls on chickens

source.title: ACE, Global meal replacement estimates (2024), 'SADs per year (global)' tab
source.note: Farmed birds 11.62 a year × 15.73 SADs (mean of broiler 2.53 and laying hen 28.94): 183 of 2,819 SADs a year.

rows.explainer: The share of a replaced meal's suffering-adjusted days that falls on farmed birds, counted as chickens. See the fish share for the source and caveats.

rows.label: Share of a replaced meal's suffering that falls on pigs and other mammals

source.title: ACE, Global meal replacement estimates (2024), 'SADs per year (global)' tab
source.note: Farmed mammals 0.61 a year × 59.7 SADs (mean of piglet 34.85 and sow 84.55): 36 of 2,819 SADs a year.

rows.explainer: The share of a replaced meal's suffering-adjusted days that falls on farmed mammals, which ACE counts as pigs. See the fish share for the source and caveats.

rows.label: Fall in production per unit fall in consumption (cumulative elasticity factor)

source.title: Norwood and Lusk (2011), Compassion, by the Pound, figure 8.2, as reproduced by Brian Tomasik

rows.explainer:
When someone eats one pound less chicken, prices fall a little and other people buy a little more, so total consumption, and therefore production, falls by less than a pound. Norwood and Lusk estimate 0.76 lb for chicken, 0.74 for pork, 0.68 for beef, 0.56 for milk and 0.91 eggs per egg.

Best guess is chicken's, since chickens and fish dominate the animal count of a typical replaced meal; the range spans milk (0.56) to eggs (0.91). Diet-change models multiply by this; ACE's models don't, which is one reason charityevals' diet-change results can run lower than ACE's.
